mentions.name: MCP Server Security Index
mentions.description: A free browsable index of MCP servers, automatically scored for security and enterprise suitability. It periodically collects MCP servers and every new version from the Official MCP registry and assigns each a score based on 29 distinct criteria, including runtime guardrails (destructive tools, over-broad permissions, rug pulls), SAST scans, and transport & trust model. The index surfaces findings such as 1 in 10 servers being essentially unusable (score 40/100 or below), 18% of popular servers with 1000+ GitHub stars containing security issues, and 184 servers that changed their tool definitions after publication, which may indicate a rug pull attack. Browsing is free; requesting an API key enables automated, programmatic lookups for any workflow.
mentions.problem: Manually approving or rejecting MCP servers for enterprise use made the security team a bottleneck to AI adoption, so the process is automated with continuous scoring from the Official MCP registry.
mentions.audience: Security-minded people who want to be at the forefront of AI adoption, and security teams tired of being called the bottleneck.
mentions.source_excerpt:
https://index.canopii.dev

Part of my job is to approve / reject MCP servers based on how secure they are and whether they are suitable for use in an enterprise environment. I was tired of my team being called the bottleneck to AI adoption, so I set out to automate the whole process.

I periodically collect the MCP servers and every new version from the Official MCP registry and assign them a score based on 29 distinct criteria like runtime guardrails (e.g. destructive tools, over broad permissions, rug pulls), SAST scans and transport & trust model.
mentions.author: mavzer
